knowledge:
- key_parameters: dat=A flowFrame object containing the flow cytometry data to be transformed ;; fun=The transformation function to apply, which must be one of "mclMultivBoxCox", "mclMultivArcSinh", "mclMultivBiexp", or "mclMultivLinLog" ;; dims=A character vector specifying the dimensions/channels of the flowFrame to transform ;; n2f=A logical value indicating whether to perform negative-to-figure conversion (typically FALSE) ;; parameters.only=A logical value; if TRUE, only the optimized transformation parameters are returned; if FALSE, both the transformed flowFrame and the parameters are returned
- alternatives: Using default transformation parameters in flowCore, which do not adapt to the specific dataset and can result in higher variability in cell population locations across samples
- when_to_use: Use this package when preparing flow cytometry data for gating or clustering, especially in high-throughput experiments where sample-to-sample variation in optimal transformation parameters needs to be minimized by data-dependent optimization
- pitfalls: Optimal transformation parameters are highly data-dependent and can vary significantly between samples; inverse transformations are not fully integrated as S4 classes in this version, requiring manual tracking of parameters if inverse operations are needed

workflows.name: flow_cytometry_transformation_optimization
workflows.intent: Optimize transformation parameters for flow cytometry channels to achieve multivariate normality and transform the data.
input: flowFrame.rds (A flowFrame object containing flow cytometry measurements)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the flow cytometry data ;; 2. Run flowTrans to optimize parameters and transform the selected dimensions ;; 3. Extract the optimized parameters for downstream use ;; 4. Plot the untransformed and transformed data to visually inspect the results ;; 5. Run flowTrans with parameters.only=TRUE to obtain parameters for integration into flowCore workflows
